Purola, V.M. (2021). Heat integration in a hydrocarbon processing facility. US Patent Application Publication US 2021/0171836 A1, published 10 June 2021; Appl. No. 17/116,660, filed 9 December 2020 (provisional 62/945,469, filed 9 December 2019). Applicant: Coolbrook Oy, Helsinki, Finland.

Loaded: the four comparative energy and material balance simulations (Examples 1-4, Tables 1-4) of a 1000 kt/a naphtha ethylene plant: conventional fired cracker versus rotary (rotodynamic, Coolbrook RDR) reactor plants with fired preheat, electric preheat, MP steam import and H2/O2 direct heating. Every per-t value is per t ethylene (all plant energy charged to ethylene), derived from printed MW and t/h (ethylene 119.1 t/h in all cases), arithmetic in formula. Net energy consumption = total energy minus HP steam export credit; the printed fuel gas export (MW) is NOT subtracted and differs strongly between cases (86 MW conventional vs 372-862 MW RDR), so part of the RDR saving is feed-derived fuel gas shifted from burning to export; it is recorded in _flows. Example 1 Case B electricity is inferred from paras [0212]/[0217], which treat its 531 MW net consumption as electricity. Example 4: hydrogen fuel energy excluded by the patent. CO2 is inside battery limit, fuel fired, with CO2-free electricity. Products per t ethylene in _flows (ethylene yield on naphtha 35.1 wt% conventional, 42.2 wt% RDR in Examples 1, 3, 4). Background statements (furnace efficiency 92-95% NHV reprinted from Ullmann; CO2 1.0-1.2 / 1.8-2.0 t per t ethylene for ethane / naphtha) loaded under a background process. No costs and no TRL in the patent. Locators: printed patent page numbers (text pages 1-15 as printed in the page header; drawing sheets not numbered as pages) plus paragraph numbers. The PDF is an OCR image of the publication; all table values were cross-checked against the uspto.report HTML copy of the same publication (kept as STEM.mhtml). Table 3 prints the conventional CO2 as 144852 kg/h against 144844 in Tables 1-2 (both as printed; Table 1 value used).
